item.title: WES BORLAND Says LIMP BIZKIT Has 'Ammo' For New Music As Seventh Studio Album Starts Taking Shape
item.description: Limp Bizkit appear to be back in the studio, putting fresh weight behind the possibility that the band’s long-discussed seventh studio album is finally moving forward. Recent photos and reports place Fred Durst, Wes Borland and other members working with producer Benjamin Grizzell in Nashville, just as the group enjoys one of the busiest periods of its career.

item.title: JAMES LABRIE Reveals What It’s Really Like Having MIKE PORTNOY Back In DREAM THEATER
item.description: DREAM THEATER singer James LaBrie recently shared his thoughts on the band’s monumental reunion with founding drummer Mike Portnoy, stating that after a few initial shows, the feeling of having him back was no longer “surreal” but simply “right.

item.title: Dino Cazares Says Milo Silvestro Brings Back Classic Fear Factory Sound: 'He Delivers Every Night'
item.description: FEAR FACTORY guitarist and mastermind Dino Cazares has once again praised the band’s new vocalist, Milo Silvestro, saying the Italian-born singer is “reminiscent of what Burton sounded like” in the band’s heyday.

item.title: SLASH Announces New Album With Myles Kennedy & The Conspirators: 'Best One Yet'
item.description: Slash Featuring Myles Kennedy & The Conspirators have wrapped recording on their fifth album. The catch? You won’t hear it until 2027. On August 28, Slash posted a photo with bassist Todd Kerns and drummer Brent Fitz on Instagram, announcing the sessions were complete.

item.title: Killswitch Engage's JESSE LEACH Reflects On Tour Life: 'We Owe It To The Fans, Dude'
item.description: Killswitch Engage singer Jesse Leach opened up about the pressures of touring and how he protects his voice on the road. In a recent interview with American Musical Supply, Leach explained his routine for staying healthy and keeping his vocals in shape while traveling.

item.title: MORGAN LANDER Explains Why KITTIE No Longer Fits The 'Nu Metal' Label: 'We’re Not Trying To Recapture The Past'
item.description: Kittie frontwoman Morgan Lander says the band has outgrown the nu metal tag. In a new interview with Metalshop TV, the guitarist and vocalist said that calling Kittie a nu metal band no longer fits what they sound like.

item.title: Deftones Announce 2026 European and UK Tour With Denzel Curry and Drug Church
item.description: Deftones are heading back to Europe in 2026. The Sacramento-based alternative metal band has confirmed a 15-date arena tour across Europe and the United Kingdom in support of their upcoming album Private Music.

item.title: FIT FOR A KING Announces New Album 'LONELY GOD', Shares Lead Single And Tracklist
item.description: Fit For A King have unveiled Lonely God, their eighth studio album, scheduled to arrive August 1, 2025 via Solid State Records. The announcement came with a music video (available at the end of this article) for the blistering title track, which showcases the band’s signature blend of gnarly riffs, guttural growls, heavy grooves, and a dash of industrial crunch.

item.title: BRIAN WELCH on KORN's New Album: 'We're Doing It All On Tape'
item.description: Korn is back in the studio, but don’t expect any instant gratification. This time, they’re ditching modern convenience for a much older, sweatier process. During a chat with BBC Radio 1’s Rock Show With Daniel P Carter (as transcribed by The PRP, guitarist Brian “Head” Welch explained that the band has fully embraced analog recording.

item.title: PIGGY D. On Working With MARILYN MANSON: 'I'm Proud To Stand Next To Him'
item.description: Matt Montgomery, better known as Piggy D., isn’t shy when it comes to describing his experience playing bass for Marilyn Manson. In a recent interview with Radioactive MikeZ on 96.

item.title: DAVE MUSTAINE starts recording vocals as MEGADETH’s 17th studio album nears completion
item.description: The next Megadeth record has been crawling toward completion for months. Since the release of The Sick, The Dying… and the Dead! back in 2022, work on its successor has quietly advanced.

item.title: Kirk Hammett Rules Out Retirement From Metallica Despite 62 Years of Age
item.description: Kirk Hammett has no interest in slowing down. Speaking to Metal Hammer, he dismissed the idea of retirement entirely. “I don’t believe in retirement. Retirement is something that’s been forced onto people; I don’t believe musicians are allowed to retire,” he said.
